scenes.narration: Every device has its own clock, and they all drift. Logs from different devices stop lining up. N T P keeps every clock in step.

scenes.heading: The town clock
scenes.narration: Think of a town clock that everyone sets their pocket watch by. The most accurate source is stratum zero, like an atomic clock. Each step away adds one to the stratum number. Sixteen means the device isn't in sync at all. It all runs over U D P port one two three.

scenes.heading: Setting it up
scenes.narration: Setup is short. Point the device at a time server. Turn on authentication. Check the status. And check who it's syncing with.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. That command makes it a client. You must also turn on authentication. Only use master when there's no better source.

items.wrong: ntp server makes it a server

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. N T P keeps clocks in sync over U D P one two three. Lower stratum means closer to the source. Stratum sixteen means unsynchronised. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva NTP lab.
